title.en: Prism, dispersion, atmospheric refraction and scattering

text.en: After rain, a rainbow appears; at sunset the sky turns red. Both come from the behaviour of light in the atmosphere and in glass.

A glass prism refracts light twice and bends it toward its base. The angle of deviation depends on the angle of incidence.
Newton showed that white light is dispersed into seven colours VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
Violet bends the most and red bends the least, because different colours travel with different speeds in glass.
A rainbow forms by dispersion, internal reflection and refraction of sunlight in raindrops. It is seen when the Sun is behind the observer.
Atmospheric refraction makes stars twinkle and the Sun appear about two minutes before sunrise and after sunset.
Scattering of light by particles: Tyndall effect shows the path of a beam through a colloid, like sunlight through mist.
The sky is blue because shorter wavelengths scatter more. At sunrise and sunset light travels a longer path, blue is scattered away and red reaches us.
Danger signals are red because red scatters the least and can be seen from far away.

problem.en: Why do stars twinkle but planets do not?

text.en: Starlight refracts through layers of changing density, so the apparent position shifts.
Stars are point sources, so the shift changes the brightness.
Planets are extended sources, so the variations average out.

points.en: White light disperses into VIBGYOR; violet bends the most and red the least.
Sky is blue due to scattering; sunsets are red.
Stars twinkle due to atmospheric refraction.
